messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-demo: FintechCo performance / SLO checklist and next steps

Hi Sarah / Chris —

Great session today, thanks for the time. Per our demo and the perf discussion with Vivek, I wanted to capture the performance/SLO items we discussed and propose next steps so we stay aligned for the POC decision. Attached is a short PDF recap and an editable SLO checklist.

High-level SLOs you called out during the demo:
- P95 latency target: <= 350ms (text-gen baseline, 2k token context)
- P99 latency target: <= 700ms (non-streaming worst-case)
- Start-of-stream latency (streaming): <= 200ms for first partial token
- Throughput target: 100-150 requests/sec sustained for peak windows
- Concurrency target: support ~16 concurrent active sessions per shard
- Streaming support: chunked token streaming with keepalive and chunk size ~512 tokens

What we need from you to validate during the perf run:
1) Sample production-like payloads (2-3 payload shapes) + average tokens per request
2) Expected concurrency pattern (steady vs spiky) and any burst diagrams
3) Desired model version (we demoed redwood-2-3b-quant) and whether quantized variants are acceptable
4) Network egress location / VPC peering details for latency estimates

Proposed next steps / MAP items:
- Marissa: coordinate scheduling for a 2-hour perf validation window with your Infra (target week of 7/27) - owner: marissa_cole
- Vivek: perf-run plan + test harness and metrics dashboard (we'll include token-level latency, P50/P95/P99, and streaming jitter) - owner: vivek_kulkarni
- FintechCo Infra: share sample payloads and a run window; confirm any firewall/egress rules - owner: Sarah Patel / Chris Wu
- Lauren: executive checklist for SLA decision criteria (if the run meets targets, proposed path to canary) - owner: lauren_bishop

Please review the attached checklist and confirm (1) the SLO numbers above, (2) availability for the perf run week of 7/27, and (3) any additional success criteria we should include.

Thanks -

--Marissa

Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FintechCo performance / SLO checklist and next steps

Thanks Marissa - this is super helpful and captures the convo. A few clarifications from our side after syncing with infra: 

- Latency: P95 <= 350ms is our target; P99 <= 800ms is acceptable as a stretch (our internal SLA is P99 < 1s).
- Streaming: need first-token start within 200ms for the paywall preview feature; sustained stream throughput must not exceed 150ms per chunk on average.
- Throughput/concurrency: we'll aim to validate at 120 req/sec with up to 20 concurrent sessions (some of our sessions are long-lived).
- Model: we prefer the redwood-2-3b-quant path if it meets latency - otherwise happy to test the full fp16 variant for baseline.

We can provide sample payloads by EOD Friday (7/23). For perf window, 7/27 afternoon PST works for us. Please include the exact harness steps you need (we'd like a runbook).

On success criteria: if P95 < 350ms and start-of-stream < 200ms with no more than 1% error rate during the test and sustained 120 req/sec for 20m, that would be a green light for a canary.

--Sarah
Sarah Patel | Director, Product - FintechCo
sarah@fintechco.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FintechCo performance / SLO checklist and next steps

Thanks - noted. I'll put together the perf-run plan and the harness repo (we use a small k6 + custom streaming client for tokenized load). High-level plan:

- Day 0 (prep): get sample payloads + network details + model variant to test
- Day 1 (smoke): low-volume sanity checks, verify streaming path and first-token latencies
- Day 1 (run): ramp to 120 req/sec sustained for 20 minutes, run 3 iterations to check stability
- Metrics: collect per-token latency, P50/P95/P99, error rate, connection churn, and throughput. We'll share a live Grafana dashboard link during the run.

Questions for FintechCo: can you share an origin IP range for the perf-run so we can pre-authorize ACLs? Also confirm if the traffic will originate from your VPC or via a test harness hosted by Redwood (we can do either).

I'll upload the harness and a short runbook to the Drive link Marissa shared by EOD today.

--Vivek
